Bellweather Begins Three-Year Tree Canopy Project

The fictional city of Bellweather began planting the first of 2,400 trees on March 18, 2027, as part of a three-year effort to cool neighborhoods with sparse shade. Mayor Elena Ruiz announced the Canopy Corridors program at Harbor Park, where crews planted twelve coast live oaks along Mason Avenue.

City forester Dev Malik said the first phase will focus on four census tracts where summer surface temperatures averaged six degrees higher than the citywide reading in a 2026 survey. He cautioned that the survey covered only clear afternoons and should not be treated as a complete measure of residents' heat exposure.

The council approved $1.8 million for planting and two years of maintenance on February 27. According to budget director Nia Cole, a regional grant will cover about half the cost, although the final award has not yet been signed. Residents may request a street tree beginning April 2. Officials expect the first 700 plantings to be complete by December, weather permitting.
